To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of the health conditions studied was significantly higher in drinkers compared with nondrinkers, and that the prevalence was significantly reduced in those who had stopped drinking alcohol.

alcohol consumption was positively associated with the risk of incident diabetes and that the association was modified by the presence of metabolic syndrome and by the amount and frequency of drinking.

the most common health conditions reported by drinkers who quit drinking were: (i) cardiovascular diseases; (ii) musculoskeletal diseases and injuries; and (iii) mental and behavioral disorders, including alcohol use disorder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the consumption of alcohol on the health of the population, with a focus on the health of people aged 45 and over.
the relationship between the consumption of alcohol and the incidence of health conditions in a sample of 97,852 drinkers aged 45 years or older who participated in the 45 and Up Study.
the relationship between the use of alcohol and the use of other drugs and alcohol-related health conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alcohol is harmful to the health of individuals and society.
the use of alcohol is a risk factor for a number of diseases and conditions, and is also a cause of death.
alcohol consumption has a positive impact on the health of the human being.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the health benefits of alcohol consumption are small compared with the health risks and, with moderate drinking at best, the overall balance of risks and benefits is negative.
the results of our research suggest that the relationship between alcohol consumption and health conditions is not straightforward.
the results of this research indicate that the majority of drinkers who cease drinking alcohol do so for reasons other than a health concern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alcohol consumption cessation is associated with a number of health benefits for older drinkers.
alcohol consumption cessation is associated with an improvement in health conditions, and that this association is stronger among people aged over 45.
